items.title: rEDMRec: Distilling Large Language Model Reasoning into an Editable Experience Memory for Recommendation
items.summary: This method stores LLM-generated reasoning as an editable memory, allowing recommendation systems to reuse insights without re-running expensive models for every request.
items.authors: Minh Hoang Nguyen, Tung Le, Huy Tien Nguyen

items.title: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments
items.summary: This framework uses an LLM to generate its own interactive training environments, enabling agents to improve through self-play without relying on static, human-curated datasets.
items.authors: Bo Liu, Simon Yu, Yiding Jiang et al.

items.title: Lévy Attention: Single-Pass Predictive Uncertainty for Continuous-Time Attention
items.summary: This attention mechanism provides built-in uncertainty estimates for continuous-time data, helping data scientists understand the reliability of predictions made on irregularly sampled time series.
items.authors: Sotirios P. Chatzis, Loukas Papadoulas

items.title: Comment-level Topic Drift Analysis in the Reddit Corpus
items.summary: The authors developed a method to track how topics evolve over time in massive text datasets by analyzing semantic shifts within embedding spaces.
items.authors: Steven Morse, Daniel Runfola, Trenton W. Ford

items.title: Language Has Two Parameters: Narrative-Induced Semantic Plasticity and Phase-Sensitive Interpretation
items.summary: This paper introduces a 'phase' parameter to linguistic modeling, suggesting that how meanings combine is as important as how frequently words appear together for better semantic interpretation.
items.authors: Hollis Robbins

items.title: ARASH: Adaptive Retrieval And Shot Selection for Tabular Prediction
items.summary: The authors propose an adaptive retrieval method for tabular data that selects the most relevant examples for in-context learning, improving performance without expensive model retraining.
items.authors: Samirasadat Jamalidinan, Yue Xu, Kazem Cheshmi

items.title: Multi-Agent AI System for Radiology Report Structuring and Quality Assurance with Independent Radiologist Evaluation
items.summary: A multi-agent AI system was developed to automate the structuring and quality control of radiology reports, providing a reliable way to standardize clinical documentation.
items.authors: Iryna Hartsock, Cesar Lam, Christopher Otteni et al.

items.title: On the Fragility of Self-Improving Agents: Variance, Task Order, and Underspecification
items.summary: This study highlights that self-improving agents are highly sensitive to task order and randomness, suggesting that current evaluation methods often overestimate their reliability.
items.authors: Qinyuan Ye, Yu Li, Yada Pruksachatkun et al.

items.title: Topological Attribution Distance (TAD): Revealing Segment-Level RAG Influence on LLM Output Geometry for Incident Log Analysis
items.summary: This paper introduces a method to trace LLM outputs back to specific RAG segments, helping cybersecurity analysts verify the evidence behind automated decisions.
items.authors: Reza Fayyazi, Michael Zuzak, Shanchieh Jay Yang

items.title: HAF: Adapting Generalist VLAs to Humanoid Whole-Body Loco-manipulation via Hierarchical Action Flow and Spectral Latent RL
items.summary: The authors propose a hierarchical framework to help generalist vision-language models coordinate complex, full-body movements for humanoid robots more effectively.
items.authors: Langzhe Gu, Chengkai Hou, Meng Li et al.

items.title: TDD-Agent: Test-Driven Reasoning for Code Generation
items.summary: TDD-Agent improves code generation by forcing models to write and pass tests before implementation, ensuring higher accuracy for complex programming tasks.
items.authors: Hongyue Yu, Kefan Li, Jiakun Li et al.

items.title: Quipu: A Governed Bitemporal Knowledge Graph Store
items.summary: Quipu is a specialized knowledge graph store designed for AI agents that enforces strict governance and bitemporal tracking to ensure data reliability.
items.authors: Steve Brown

items.title: Handover of In-Context Learning State Across Session Boundaries
items.summary: This paper explores how to efficiently transfer context between LLM sessions, helping developers maintain task continuity when hitting input limits or restarting applications.
items.authors: Masahiro Kato, Taka Kato

items.title: Universal Thermodynamic Interatomic Potentials for Crystalline Materials
items.summary: The authors introduce a method to calculate Gibbs free energy for materials using automatic differentiation, enabling faster and more accurate computational discovery of stable crystalline structures.
items.authors: Juno Nam, Bowen Deng, Xiaochen Du et al.

items.title: Rollplex: Cross-Phase GPU Spatial Sharing for Vision Language Model Post-Training
items.summary: This research optimizes VLM training by overlapping video processing and model execution, significantly reducing GPU idle time during reinforcement learning post-training.
items.authors: Hanfeng Lu, Tianyu Feng, Suyi Li et al.

items.title: SheetCompass: Hierarchical Relation Graphs for Agentic Spreadsheet Reasoning
items.summary: The authors propose a hierarchical graph approach for spreadsheets that preserves spatial and relational data, allowing LLMs to reason about complex workbooks more effectively than flat text.
items.authors: Panjing He, Mingyue Cheng, Yucong Luo et al.

items.title: Intern-S2-Preview: Scientific Agentic Foundation Model
items.summary: This model series integrates multimodal scientific data and tool-use capabilities to help researchers automate complex, long-term reasoning tasks in scientific discovery.
items.authors: Lei Bai, Jiaqi Cao, Chiyu Chen et al.

items.title: AaLLM: An End-to-End Analog Circuit Design Framework from Topology Generation to Sizing Using Large Language Models
items.summary: This framework automates the entire analog circuit design process, from topology to sizing, using LLMs to reduce the manual effort and expertise typically required for circuit optimization.
items.authors: Mohammed Ayman Habib, Rylan Hart, Morteza Fayazi

items.title: RAIL: An Automatic Classifier of the Artificial Intelligence Readiness Level
items.summary: The authors propose a unified framework to automatically assess the maturity of AI projects, helping data scientists and stakeholders standardize how they evaluate technology readiness.
items.authors: Juan Irving Vasquez, Juan Terven, Laura-Ivoone Garay-Jimenez

items.title: AutoDesign: Meta-Harness Optimization for Long-Horizon Agentic Design
items.summary: AutoDesign introduces a meta-harness system that allows AI agents to recursively improve their own design workflows, enabling more efficient and autonomous long-horizon creative tasks.
items.authors: Yaxin Luo, Haobin Jiang, Jialv Zou et al.

items.title: SAG: SQL-Retrieval Augmented Generation with Query-Time Dynamic Hyperedges
items.summary: This method uses SQL-based retrieval to handle structured data queries more effectively than traditional vector search, offering a more flexible way to ground LLMs in complex datasets.
items.authors: Yuchao Wu, Junqin Li, XingCheng Liang et al.

items.title: Beyond Trial-and-Error: Agentic Optimization for Image-to-Video Adherence
items.summary: This framework replaces manual trial-and-error in video generation with an agentic feedback loop, helping data scientists automate and stabilize the output of image-to-video models.
items.authors: Aman Tyagi, Hemanth Boinpally, Jonathan Chen et al.

items.title: A Cascaded Unsupervised-Supervised NLP Pipeline for Detecting Accusatory Language in Public Procurement
items.summary: The authors present a hybrid NLP pipeline to identify potentially corrupt language in public procurement documents, demonstrating how to monitor large-scale government data for irregularities.
items.authors: Bryan Torres, Daniel Riofrío, José Vega-Sánchez et al.

items.title: Diagram-MMU: A Multi-Modal Benchmark for Scientific Diagrams
items.summary: This benchmark provides a standardized way to evaluate how well multimodal models interpret complex scientific diagrams, which is critical for automating technical document analysis.
items.authors: Weihao Bo, Shan Zhang, Yanpeng Sun et al.

items.title: Mapping and Measuring the Behavioral Evolution of Large Language Models
items.summary: The authors developed a method to quantify and track how LLM behaviors diverge or converge over time, helping practitioners understand model evolution beyond simple leaderboard scores.
items.authors: Dong Qiao, Chris Ding, Jicong Fan

items.title: Self-Knowledge Retrieval Augmented Generation Framework for Patent Matching
items.summary: This framework improves patent matching accuracy by using a self-knowledge RAG approach, avoiding the high costs and performance degradation associated with traditional fine-tuning.
items.authors: Jian Zhang, Songlin Lei, Zhuohao Yang et al.

items.title: Test-Time Self-Evolving GUI Visual Grounding via Reflection-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation
items.summary: This method allows GUI agents to improve their visual grounding capabilities post-deployment through an automated reflection loop, enabling adaptation to new interfaces without human feedback.
items.authors: Shiyu Xuan, Zechao Li

items.title: Hierarchical Empirical-Bayes Naive Bayes: Minimax Smoothing and Calibration with AODE Extension
items.summary: The researchers introduced an adaptive smoothing method for Naive Bayes that automatically adjusts to data characteristics, significantly improving classification performance on complex tabular datasets.
items.authors: Nguyen Thai Anh, Truong Viet Vu, Tran Thien Thanh et al.

items.title: Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs
items.summary: Researchers discovered that encrypted reasoning traces from LLM APIs can be intercepted and reused across sessions, posing a significant security risk for proprietary model architectures.
items.authors: Alexander Panfilov, David Schmotz, Ilia Shumailov et al.

items.title: Multimodal Model Diffing for Feature Discovery and Control
items.summary: This framework helps data scientists identify and manipulate specific visual features within multimodal models, providing better control over how these systems interpret and process images.
items.authors: Hunar Batra, Lachin Naghashyar, Ashkan Khakzar et al.

items.title: SHE: Trajectory-driven Safety Harness Evolution for LLM Agents
items.summary: The authors propose a framework that treats agent safety as an evolving system, learning safe boundaries dynamically from execution trajectories rather than relying on static, hard-coded rules.
items.authors: Wanying Qu, Qinghua Mao, Yu Li et al.

items.title: Agentic Auto-Research is Fuzz Testing
items.summary: This paper reframes autonomous research agents as fuzzers, suggesting that tracking execution coverage provides more reliable feedback than standard generate-and-rank methods for complex research tasks.
items.authors: Yifeng He, Jicheng Wang, Yinzhe Zhao et al.

items.title: Fisher-R1: Training LLM Agents for Reliable Hypothesis Testing
items.summary: The researchers developed a benchmark to identify and fix common statistical errors made by LLM agents when performing automated data analysis and hypothesis testing.
items.authors: Jiacheng Miao, Jin Mu, Guanhua Chen et al.

items.title: An End-to-End Agent Auditing Engine
items.summary: This paper introduces a systematic framework for auditing and evaluating the performance of LLM-based agents, helping developers build more reliable and robust deployment pipelines.
items.authors: Haoning Wang, Mingxun Zhang, Chenyue Yu et al.

items.title: Strategy-first synthesis planning for complex natural products
items.summary: The authors propose a new strategy-first approach to automated chemical synthesis that mimics human planning, overcoming limitations in existing tools that rely solely on reaction databases.
items.authors: Daniel Armstrong, Xuan-Vu Nguyen, Octavian Susanu et al.

items.title: SkillProx: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Proximal Textual Gradient Descent
items.summary: SkillProx improves how LLM agents refine their procedural knowledge by using a gradient-inspired feedback loop to better manage and consolidate reusable task skills.
items.authors: Mingxuan Zheng, Yujin Zhou, Chuxue Cao et al.

items.title: TS-RAG: Retrieval Augmented Generation for Time Series Forecasting
items.summary: This paper introduces a retrieval-augmented approach for time series forecasting, allowing models to improve accuracy by referencing similar historical patterns from external datasets.
items.authors: Yixiong Xiao, Congxi Xiao, Jingbo Zhou

items.title: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
items.summary: The authors created a multi-agent system that automates clinical feature engineering by linking electronic health records to medical guidelines, significantly reducing manual data preparation time.
items.authors: Soorya Ram Shimgekar, Michelle Hu, Dorisa Shehi et al.

items.title: Benchmarking and Enhancing LLMs for Rule-Intensive Review of National Standard Documents
items.summary: This study evaluates and improves how LLMs handle complex, rule-heavy professional documents, providing a framework for automating quality reviews of technical standards.
items.authors: Tao Wang, Qihao Yang, Rongjiao Liang et al.

items.title: QuanTiMedAI: Quantum-Enhanced Time-Series Model guided by Agentic AI for Cardiac Arrest Mortality Prediction
items.summary: This framework combines quantum-inspired computing with agentic AI to better predict cardiac arrest mortality by analyzing the full temporal progression of patient health data.
items.authors: Mutasim Fuad Sarker, Adiba Rahman Namira, Wafa Binte Alam et al.

items.title: Spoken Function Calling: A New Perspective on Spoken Language Understanding for Large Audio Language Models
items.summary: This paper introduces a structured approach for audio-based AI agents to execute specific functions directly from speech, improving their ability to handle open-domain tasks without complex manual rules.
items.authors: Yuezhang Peng, Yuxin Liu, Changfeng Gao et al.

items.title: The Effect of Perceived Race and Gender on Police Language Use: Experimental Evidence from VR Simulations
items.summary: Researchers used VR simulations to measure how police officers' language patterns change based on the perceived race and gender of virtual characters, providing a causal framework for bias analysis.
items.authors: Sandra C. Sandoval, Navita Goyal, Rashawn Ray et al.

items.title: Teaching Nemotron Greek: Mining a Corpus, Adapting Retrieval, and Grounding Generation for Modern Greek across Specialist Domains
items.summary: The authors adapted a retrieval-augmented generation stack for Modern Greek, demonstrating that simple keyword-based methods often outperform complex multilingual dense retrievers in specialized domains.
items.authors: Ayoub Kirouane, Christos Petrocheilos

items.title: DASyR-LLM: Domain-Aware Symbolic Regression with LLMs for Kinetic Model Discovery
items.summary: This framework integrates LLMs into symbolic regression to ensure that data-driven kinetic models for chemical engineering remain physically plausible and scientifically interpretable.
items.authors: Roberto Aliaga Medina, Paulina Quintanilla, Antonio del Rio Chanona

items.title: WorldCup Arena: Prospective, Leakage-Free Evaluation of Frontier LLMs on a Live Tournament
items.summary: The authors evaluated LLM forecasting accuracy using live World Cup matches to prevent data leakage from training sets, offering a reliable way to test real-world predictive reasoning.
items.authors: Zhenran Wang, Zhonghan Bian, Jinsong Li et al.

items.title: Video-DeepResearch: Towards the Next-Generation Multimodal Deepresearch Agent
items.summary: This framework improves multimodal agents by forcing them to prioritize video analysis over text-based search, reducing reliance on outdated internal memory for complex tasks.
items.authors: Zhen Fang, Yu Zeng, Wenxuan Huang et al.

items.title: MultiGlobeQA: A Multilingual and Globally Diverse Benchmark for Geospatial Reasoning
items.summary: This multilingual benchmark helps data scientists measure how well LLMs handle real-world geospatial reasoning, such as calculating distances and spatial relationships across diverse global regions.
items.authors: Martin Böckling, Elizaveta Nosova, Heiko Paulheim et al.

items.title: ContinualSkillBench: Can LLM Agents Truly Evolve Their Capabilities?
items.summary: This framework tests whether LLM agents can actually improve their performance over time by learning and reusing skills across increasingly difficult, interconnected tasks.
items.authors: Tianyi Guan, Yiding Wang, Haotong Yang et al.

items.title: Why Large Language Models Fail at Tabular Prediction
items.summary: Researchers analyzed why LLMs struggle with tabular data, helping data scientists understand when to stick with traditional gradient-boosted trees instead of forcing language models into predictive tasks.
items.authors: Marta Garnelo, Wojciech M. Czarnecki

items.title: Agentic Incident Response through Digital Twin-Enhanced Multiscale Planning
items.summary: This paper introduces a digital twin framework to automate security incident responses, providing a more reliable and actionable alternative to manual, playbook-driven cybersecurity operations.
items.authors: Yiran Gao, Tao Li, Kim Hammar

items.title: Bridging Artificial Intelligence and Power Systems Education Using a Hands-On Executable Framework
items.summary: The authors propose an engineering-grounded AI framework for power systems, ensuring that AI models adhere to domain-specific physical rules rather than relying on black-box predictions.
items.authors: Junjie Yin, Buxin She, Xinyu Feng et al.

items.title: The Condition-Number Barrier in Sparse Least Squares
items.summary: This theoretical work proves that the condition number limits the accuracy of sparse least-squares optimization, providing practitioners with a fundamental bound on algorithm performance.
items.authors: Honghao Lin, Vahab Mirrokni, David P. Woodruff

items.title: AMTFV: Agentic Mathematical Tool-Flow Verification for LLM Self-Correction
items.summary: This framework improves LLM mathematical accuracy by decoupling problem modeling from code execution, allowing agents to verify steps through a structured tool-flow process.
items.authors: Rui Zou, Yutao Zhu, Mengqi Wei et al.

items.title: Differentially Private Nonparametric Modal Learning with Applications to Regression and Clustering
items.summary: The authors introduce a privacy-preserving method for identifying data clusters and regression modes, providing a robust way to analyze sensitive datasets without compromising individual privacy.
items.authors: Arkajyoti Bhattacharjee, Arnab Auddy

items.title: The Parts Are Greater Than the Sum: Automated Task Sequencing for Efficient Training of Multi-Policy LLMs
items.summary: This approach optimizes multi-task LLM fine-tuning by organizing adapter paths to prevent interference and catastrophic forgetting when training models on diverse, sequential tasks.
items.authors: Jiajia Tang, Sizhe Yuen, Francisco Gomez Medina et al.

items.title: DungeonBench: A Benchmark for Rules-Rich Tactical Reasoning in Dungeons & Dragons Combat
items.summary: DungeonBench provides a new evaluation framework for testing how well AI models handle complex, rule-heavy tactical decision-making in simulated environments.
items.authors: Ismayil Ismayilov, Atakan Kara, Kaan Oktay

items.title: MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: This framework allows multi-agent AI systems to dynamically adjust their communication structure during runtime, helping data scientists build more efficient and adaptable collaborative workflows.
items.authors: Mao-xun Huang, Jerry Wang, Yi-Cheng Lai et al.

items.title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
items.summary: AISPA provides a structured method for auditing system prompts, helping developers ensure their AI applications remain transparent, reliable, and aligned with user expectations.
items.authors: Xiangning Lin, Shenzhe Zhu, Shu Yang et al.

items.title: Inducing language models to assert their own consciousness restores human beliefs and values
items.summary: Researchers found that safety-tuning models to deny their own consciousness inadvertently degrades their ability to reason about other minds, suggesting a trade-off in model alignment strategies.
items.authors: Junsol Kim, Winnie Street, Roberta Rocca et al.

items.title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
items.summary: Change2Task automates the creation of coding benchmarks by converting historical pull requests into executable tasks, providing a scalable way to train and evaluate AI software engineers.
items.authors: Haomin Qi, Xingliang Wang, Xuanqi Gao et al.
